title: IV iron infusion
what: Iron medicine is given through a drip into a vein. This refills your iron stores faster than tablets.
why: For iron deficiency anemia when tablets do not help or cause side effects, in pregnancy, or before surgery, as your doctor prescribes.
duration: one infusion usually takes 15 to 60 minutes, plus 30 minutes of observation; blood tests show the effect after a few weeks
tell_doctor: If you ever had an allergy to iron medicines or other medicines

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: You can usually eat as normal.

prepare.title: Tablets
prepare.text: Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide if you need iron tablets along with the infusion.

prepare.title: Clothing
prepare.text: A sleeve that is easy to roll up.

bring: Your referral and recent blood tests
steps: The nurse puts an IV line in a vein
The drip with iron is connected
It runs slowly, and you are watched
Your blood pressure and pulse are checked from time to time
After it finishes, you sit for about 30 minutes more
feel: Sometimes a metallic taste or mild nausea
A headache or muscle aches for 1 to 2 days can happen
after: A normal day. You can go home
If the medicine leaks under the skin, a brown mark can stay. So tell the nurse right away about any burning in your arm
A blood test is usually repeated after a few weeks
red_flags: During the infusion: burning in the arm, a rash, itching, shortness of breath, or dizziness. Tell the nurse right away
At home: a swollen face or trouble breathing. Call emergency services

faq.a: Tablets work more slowly and sometimes cause side effects. An infusion gives a lot of iron at once.

faq.q: How many infusions will I need?
faq.a: It depends on the medicine and how much iron you are missing. Usually 1 to 3. Your doctor decides.

reminders.text: Iron infusion today. Eat something and wear a top with an easy sleeve.
